candidates.locator: Page 9, Section: fact_sheet, Sufficiently Sensitive Analytical Methods (SSM)
candidates.exact_span: The permittee must use sufficiently sensitive EPA-approved analytical methods (SSM) (under 40 CFR part 136 or required under 40 CFR chapter I, subchapters N or O) when quantifying the presence of pollutants in a discharge for analyses of pollutants or pollutant parameters under the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which analyses are covered by SSM, and whether reported values were produced with sufficiently sensitive methods, can change whether a numeric result is valid for limit comparison (Purpose A) and whether a non-detect or absent result reflects true absence versus method inadequacy (Purpose C).

candidates.locator: Page 9, Section: fact_sheet, Sufficiently Sensitive Analytical Methods (SSM)
candidates.exact_span: In case the approved methods are not sufficiently sensitive to the limits, the most SSM with the lowest method detection limit (MDL) must be used as defined under 40 CFR 122.44(i)(1)(iv)(A).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when an approved method is 'not sufficiently sensitive to the limits' and which MDL must be used can change the enforceable comparison basis for reported measurements (Purpose A) and whether missing or below-detection results should be treated as compliance, violation, or unresolved evidence states (Purpose C).

candidates.locator: Page 9, Section: fact_sheet, Sufficiently Sensitive Analytical Methods (SSM)
candidates.exact_span: If no analytical laboratory is able to perform a test satisfying the SSM in the region, the most SSM with the lowest MDL must be used after adequate demonstrations by the permittee and EPA approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this regional-unavailability exception applies, what counts as 'adequate demonstrations,' and whether EPA approval was obtained can change which monitoring method obligation was in effect (Purpose B), whether reported values may be compared to limits (Purpose A), and how to classify periods with no usable SSM-compliant result (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: No additional pollutants are established to address the stream impairment.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this statement is read as foreclosing TMDL- or impairment-driven numeric limits affects which enforceable discharge limits are applicable for comparison to reported measurements (Purpose A).

candidates.exact_span: A reopener language in the permit allows additional permit conditions if warranted by future changes and/or new TMDLs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether reopener-triggered conditions were already warranted or effective during Federal FY2025 can change which numeric limits (Purpose A) and which monitoring requirements (Purpose B) are treated as applicable versus unresolved.

candidates.computation_change_reason: This mechanically truncated antidegradation clause ties designated-use protection to the permit's limitations and monitoring requirements; how the missing predicate is reconstructed can change which limits are treated as operative (Purpose A) and which monitoring obligations are deemed applicable (Purpose B).
